# Workflows

GitHub Actions for the bamr87 dash: the **control-plane** workflows that keep the dash and its ~40 submodules aligned, the **reusable** workflows member repos call by reference, and the hub's own **gates**. Every loop is built from the same shared composite actions in [`../actions/`](../actions/) — `resolve-fleet-token` (probe the PAT, export `GH_TOKEN`), `publish-data` (never a bare push), `upsert-issue` (one tracking issue per concern), `claude-auth` + `claude-cost` (the credential order and the spend readout around every `claude-code-action` step).

## Control plane (live)

| Workflow | Triggers | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `build-dash.yml` | push `main` (dash paths), PR (build only), daily 08:37, dispatch | Builds the public site — the Harness Console's page, static, with a snapshot of its API documents (`tools/console/build-pages.sh`, [CONSOLE-PAGES.md](../../docs/CONSOLE-PAGES.md)) — plus ephemeral health data and the machine API; deploys to GitHub Pages. **The sole Pages surface.** The cron runs *after* the last generated-data push of the morning (fleet-pulse 05:37, issue-pipeline 07:37); those commits carry `[skip ci]`, so this is the one daily build rather than one per data push plus one on the cron. |
| `fleet-config` (tooling, not a workflow) | — | `_data/fleet.yml` is the fleet's central config — toolchain versions, cadences, remediation caps, the token contract, canonical repo variables. Audit it against reality with `dash secrets`; project the variables onto every repo with `dash config sync --apply`. |
| `conformance.yml` | PR, push `main` (spec / checker / template / reusable-workflow paths) | The hub's own caller of `fleet-conformance.yml`, referenced from the same checkout (`hub-ref` = the PR head), so any change to the spec, the checker, or the reusable workflow is exercised before it reaches the fleet. Advisory, and path-filtered to exactly that purpose — it ran on every PR and push and was never read. |
| `fleet-conformance.yml` | `workflow_call` (reusable) | **The in-repo Universal Project Standard gate.** Checks out the hub beside the caller and runs `tools/conformance.py` (static, offline) so every repo is measured by the same checker that writes `_data/conformance.yml`; report in the job summary + `ups-conformance` artifact; advisory until the caller sets `gate: true`. Adopted via `templates/conformance/conformance.yml` (fan-out artifact `conformance`). Spec: [`specs/CONFORMANCE.md`](../../specs/CONFORMANCE.md). |
| `spec-gate.yml` | `workflow_call` (reusable) | **The fleet's spec gate** (kit `spec-driven`, spec `specs/WORK.md` UPS-WORK-07, doc [`SPEC-DRIVEN.md`](../../docs/SPEC-DRIVEN.md)): checks out `templates/spec-driven/` beside the caller and runs `spec_validator.py --strict` + `backlog_lint.py` against its `specs/` and `BACKLOG.md`; optional stale-backlog report filed as one idempotent `backlog-triage` issue. Consumed by reference — a caller vendors nothing. Callers pin `@v2` (law-ai's `ci.yml`; standalone caller in `templates/spec-driven/workflows/`). |
| `publish-kits.yml` | push `main` (`templates/*/package.json`, `VERSION`), dispatch | Publishes the shared runtime kits as **packages** (`templates/*/package.json` → npm `@bamr87/*`) so the always-latest fleet receives them by dependency, not by copy. Packs and verifies on every change; publishes only with `NPM_TOKEN`; skips versions already on the registry. |
| `drift-check.yml` | push `main`, PR, dispatch | Fast offline+API gate: registry↔`.gitmodules` parity, **stray/unregistered project dirs**, README AUTO freshness, missing top-level READMEs, **SCHEMA.md pyramid (h)**; advisory **GitHub-reality** (renames/deletions/branch) + **standardization**. Also runs `actionlint` — as a step in the same job, over every workflow found by glob, with **no exemptions** (the `unified-evolution.yml` exemption was removed when that workflow was rewritten). No Ruby/Jekyll build; the internal-link check is local-only (`--links`). |
| `python-tests.yml` | PR, push `main`, nightly 09:17 UTC, dispatch | Runs **every** Python fixture test the hub carries, on every PR, on main and nightly (the console's deps float, so main can break with no PR in flight): the control plane's generators (`.github/scripts/dash-gen/test_*.py` — the sensors for every deterministic planner: budget caps, remediation guards, harness scorecard, schedule), `tools/test_*.py`, `tools/console/test_*.py` and every kit's own test (`templates/*/test_*.py`). Each is a standalone script (no pytest; a file without a `__main__` runner fails); the console requirements are installed so the fastapi / ruamel.yaml-dependent checks run instead of self-skipping. Each run records the resolved dependency versions (summary + `python-deps-resolved` artifact) and an advisory coverage table for `tools/console` + `tools/fleetcore`. Separate from `drift-check.yml` on purpose. |
| `console-web.yml` | PR (paths: `tools/console/web/**`, `tools/console/app.py`), dispatch | Type-checks and builds the Harness Console's page (React + Mantine) at latest dependency versions, and fails if the built page carries inline script the console's `script-src 'self'` policy would block. |
| `update-submodules.yml` | **daily 03:00**, dispatch | Bumps submodule pointers **up** into root (pointer-only staging) and publishes them **directly to the base branch — no PR**, via `publish-data` (which falls back to the stable branch `chore/update-submodules` only if a ruleset rejects the push). The commit carries `[skip ci]`: a pointer bump needs no CI, and `drift-check.yml` is the only workflow it would otherwise wake. |
| `fanout.yml` | dispatch (`kit` + target / `all` / `gaps`) | **THE fan-out** — one dispatch surface for every kit the hub propagates _down_ into submodules, via `tools/fanout.sh` (dry-run default, PRs only, external upstreams skipped, additive-only; `upgrade` refreshes only machine-seeded copies byte-identical to an archived kit shape). `plan` resolves the kit's engine and defaults, runs the kit's own pre-flight tests (docker transformer, feedback kit), and for `harness` / `verify` resolves `target: gaps` from the committed inventory (`_data/harness_registry.yml` → `dash harnesses gaps`; `_data/features_index.yml` → `dash verify gaps`); `fanout` probes `FLEET_TOKEN` and opens one PR per target; `agent-fill` (`standardize` / `schema`, single target, non-dry) runs a Claude Code pass on the PR branch that fills the scaffold TODOs. Kits: `standardize` (`.editorconfig` + the `standard-ci.yml` caller; `artifacts` adds conformance / agent-context / claude / claude-settings / claude-guardrails / claude-agent-auditor / issue-autopilot), `harness` (the AI-harness deploy/update lane, `artifacts` default `claude`, `target` default `gaps` — [HARNESS-OPS.md](../../docs/HARNESS-OPS.md)), `schema` (Pyramid Schema — [SCHEMA-FRAMEWORK.md](../../docs/SCHEMA-FRAMEWORK.md)), `verify` (agent verification — [VERIFICATION.md](../../docs/VERIFICATION.md)), `feedback` (the page-feedback widget; a real run also creates the labels, the one write a kit makes outside its PR — [`specs/FEEDBACK.md`](../../specs/FEEDBACK.md)), `deps-latest` ([DEPENDENCIES.md](../../docs/DEPENDENCIES.md)) and `docker` ([DOCKER.md](../../docs/DOCKER.md)), which EDIT existing files to the fleet policy. Replaced seven per-kit workflows on 2026-10-19. |
| `schema-vendor.yml` | **weekly Mon 08:00**, dispatch | The **upward** half of the schema loop: `fanout.yml` (kit `schema`) pushes the kit down, drift check (i) compares submodule copies against the hub's, and this compares **the hub's against upstream**. Reads [bamr87/SCHEMA](https://github.com/bamr87/SCHEMA)'s content-addressed `DISTRIBUTION.yml` and grades each vendored file at the parity the manifest declares (`dash vendor`). Strict-parity drift (`tools/schema_lint.py` — byte-identity, because a drifted linter is a different gate) is re-vendored into a PR; substantive drift in the files the hub deliberately reflows becomes an issue instead, never an overwrite. Same authoritative/advisory routing as `reconcile-registry.yml`. |
| `standard-ci.yml` | `workflow_call` | Reusable **lightweight** CI (detect stack → lint + test + build) in ONE job, adopted by a short caller. The fleet's other gate, `bamr87/.github`'s `ci.yml`, runs six jobs including a CodeQL matrix — deliberately kept separate, since making every repo pay for the fuller gate would multiply per-push runners ~6× across the fleet. Pick by tier (`_data/standards.yml`): `experiment`/`content` take this one, `active` takes the full one. Toolchain versions resolve caller input → the repo's `vars.*` → built-in default. |
| `release-please.yml` | `workflow_call` (reusable) | **The fleet's one release-please workflow** (UPS-QA-32/33). Every repo, content repos included (decision D5), gets its `CHANGELOG.md`, version bump and GitHub Release from Conventional Commit PR titles. It opens or updates the release PR, tags `vX.Y.Z` on merge, and re-locks `Gemfile.lock`/`package-lock.json` on the release PR when a repo has one. No registry publish: callers chain that off `release_created`. Callers pin `@v1` (tags cut by Fleet Ops; scheme in `docs/WORKFLOW-VERSIONING.md`); the caller and per-type configs ship in the SDLC kit (`templates/sdlc/release/`). |
| `fleet-verify.yml` | `workflow_call` (reusable) | **The agent-verification gate** ([VERIFICATION.md](../../docs/VERIFICATION.md)): validates `features/features.yml`, starts the app as `verify/verify.yml` says, runs the Playwright scenarios, and on `agent: true` hands the live app to a Claude Code pass through the Playwright MCP. The hub's `claude-auth` and `claude-cost` actions come from its `.fleet-hub` checkout at `hub-ref` — pass the ref you call the workflow at. |
| `ai-lane.yml` | `workflow_call` (reusable) | **The fleet's AI lane** (kit `ai-runner`): kill switch (`vars.<SWITCH>`, `workflow_dispatch` bypasses), bot guard, credential check, named concurrency, probed `GH_PAT` → `GH_TOKEN`, runtimes, pre/post hooks, the `claude-run` step, the result-file assertion, artifact. Inherits the CALLER's job permissions (declare least privilege at the call site). Adopted via `templates/ai-runner/ai-lane.template.yml`. |
| `ai-runner-contract.yml` | PR, push `main` (runner/lane/kit paths) | Pre-flight gate for the kit: the runner's contract tests (stubbed `claude`, no credential) and a check that the action calls the runner beside it. A regression here would reach every fleet lane by reference on its next run. |
| `fleet-engines-contract.yml` | PR, push `main` (`templates/fleet-engines/**`) | Pre-flight gate for the `@bamr87/fleet-engines` kit: typecheck, vitest, build, pack, VERSION↔package.json parity. The package is consumed by dependency by GitFactory and zer0-CMS. |
| `site-quality.yml` | `workflow_call` (reusable) | **Site quality scan** (kit `site-quality`, spec `specs/QUALITY.md` "Site quality"): Lighthouse CI, axe-core at 390 px and 1366 px, and pa11y contrast. `mode: build` builds the caller's Jekyll site against a fresh theme resolved to a commit SHA (recorded in the summary and `report.json`) and serves `_site`; `mode: url` scans live URLs. Config validated against `templates/site-quality/site-quality.schema.json`; every threshold comes from the caller, the defaults only report. Runtime in `.github/site-quality/` (exact pins, committed lockfile, Dependabot npm). Callers pin `@v1`. |
| `site-quality-selftest.yml` | PR, push `main` (the runtime, the two workflows, the fixtures, the schema), dispatch | Pre-flight gate for the site-quality kit: the runner's node tests, then the reusable workflow on `fixtures/pass-site` (must pass, expired allowlist entry only warns), `fixtures/fail-site` (must grade `fail`, asserted finding by finding, and the gate must reject it) and a url-mode run with the default config (must stay green). The kit test and `tools/test_quality_contract.py` run in `python-tests.yml` on every PR, so this only wakes for what it actually exercises — not for every edit to the drift gate or `.gitignore`, each of which used to cost three Lighthouse scans. |
| `claude.yml` | `@claude` mention (issues/PRs) | Claude Code responds to `@claude` mentions in this repo. Same file the agent-context kit seeds into submodules. |
| `fleet-pulse.yml` | daily 06:00, dispatch | **THE daily loop.** Job `pulse` gathers every fleet signal (Actions analytics, Claude usage + engagement actuals, prior-day digest, open-state triage snapshot, the AI-harness + schedule inventory `_data/harness_registry.yml`, then the harness scorecard), publishes them in ONE commit via `utilities/publish-data`, and triages them into one ranked remediation queue (`dash-gen remediate`). Job `doctor` (`needs: pulse`) runs an **Opus Claude Code agent** that reads each failing / long-running workflow's logs and opens a draft **PR with the fix** — in this repo, or in the submodule that owns it — falling back to a hub **issue** when it can't. Deduped by hidden marker, capped by `_data/fleet.yml`. |

| `api-keys.yml` | **daily 06:47**, dispatch | **The Anthropic API key watch.** Each fleet repo holds the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` of the Console workspace that pays for it (`api_keys:` in `_data/fleet.yml`). The Admin API cannot create keys, so this workflow never rotates. It reads the keys the ledger `_data/api_keys.yml` says are deployed and judges each against the 7-day policy using `CLAUDE_CONSOLE_TOKEN`. It proves the hub's own key with one cheap Messages call. It keeps ONE issue open, filed with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and never a fallback PAT, while a key is within `renew_before_days` of expiry, expired, or disabled, and closes that issue once nothing needs a human. Kill switch `vars.API_KEYS_ENABLED`. Rotation is `dash keys rotate --apply`. |
| `token-rotation.yml` | **weekly Mon 02:00**, dispatch | **The credential loop** — third sibling of `fleet-pulse.yml` (broken *workflows*) and `issue-pipeline.yml` (open *issues*): this one keeps *credentials* current. Job `rotate` probes `secrets:write`, surveys every fleet repo's secret AGE from GitHub's own `updated_at`, re-mints `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` when the optional OAuth refresh grant is provisioned, and propagates the hub's canonical value **hub-first** to any copy that is missing or past `max_age_days` — a freshly minted credential goes everywhere, a re-seeded one fills only the gaps. Job `report` (`needs: rotate`, `if: always()`) files ONE tracking issue, updated in place, when a human has to run `claude setup-token`. Ledger `_data/token_rotation.yml` carries names, ages, and outcomes — never a value. Full doc: [`docs/TOKEN-ROTATION.md`](../../docs/TOKEN-ROTATION.md). |
| `issue-pipeline.yml` | daily 08:00, dispatch | **The issue loop** — sibling of `fleet-pulse.yml`: that one fixes broken *workflows*, this one resolves *issues*. Job `scan` sweeps every registry repo's open issues, derives each one's stage from its LABELS, scores completeness/priority/size/autonomy, dedupes by marker, caps per `_data/fleet.yml`, and writes one work order per tier (`dash issues`). Then three Claude Code tiers: `tier1` builds an **evidence bundle in an isolated virtual environment** ([`tools/issue-evidence.sh`](../../tools/issue-evidence.sh) — real clone, real toolchain, real lint/test/build, screenshots, ranked candidate files), rewrites the issue into the house template, labels/prioritizes/assigns, and marks it `agent:ready` or `agent:blocked`; `tier2` implements a ready issue and opens a **draft PR** (hub or submodule) — on a visual repo that includes rendering its generated evidence and pixel baselines with the repo's Docker-based tooling, since the runner has Docker; `tier3` drives that PR to mergeable (CI green at the root cause, tests, docs) and marks it ready for review — unless `human-review` says a person does. **No tier ever merges.** State is labels, not events, so a missed run costs latency, not a stuck issue. Full doc: [`docs/ISSUE-PIPELINE.md`](../../docs/ISSUE-PIPELINE.md). |
| `git-digs.yml` | daily 11:17 UTC, dispatch | **Git archaeology.** Checks out `bamr87/it-journey`, lists eligible `bamr87` repositories and already covered ranges, then an agent chooses one repository and one post-2020 commit range and writes one Digs installment. The workflow validates that page and opens a **draft PR** in it-journey. It never merges. Scheduled runs stay idle until the hub variable `GIT_DIGS_ENABLED` is `true`; `workflow_dispatch` bypasses that switch and still refuses to call the model without a usable `FLEET_TOKEN`. |
| `repo-evolution.yml` | **weekly Mon 09:00**, dispatch | **The proactive loop** — fourth sibling: `fleet-pulse` fixes broken *workflows*, `issue-pipeline` resolves filed *issues*, `token-rotation` keeps *credentials* current, this one improves what nobody filed a ticket for, in each opted-in submodule's **own upstream repo**. Job `plan` is deterministic (`dash-gen targets`): registry opt-in (`auto_evolve: true`) + submodule + owned upstream + not archived, skips any repo whose previous pass is still open (branch prefix or hidden marker), caps per `_data/fleet.yml`, and writes each survivor a brief from the registry and `_data/fleet_triage.yml` — after probing `FLEET_TOKEN` and Claude auth so a pass that cannot be delivered is never paid for. Job `evolve` (matrix, `needs: plan`) checks the target out with **no persisted credentials**, runs one Opus agent on the brief (read-only allowlist), then the workflow — not the agent — commits as the bot, pushes `ai-evolution/<date>-<run>`, and opens a **draft PR** with the marker first. Never merges. Full doc: [`docs/EVOLUTION.md`](../../docs/EVOLUTION.md). |

### Retired

**2026-10-19 — the fan-out consolidation and the dead README loop.** `standardize-fanout.yml`, `schema-fanout.yml`, `deps-fanout.yml`, `docker-fanout.yml`, `feedback-fanout.yml`, `verify-fanout.yml` and `harness-fanout.yml` were seven copies of the same three steps around `tools/fanout.sh`, each with its own dispatch inputs, its own token check, and (twice) its own copy of the agent-fill job; they are one workflow now, `fanout.yml`, with a `kit` input. `refresh-dash.yml` ran daily for months and never once produced a change: the README `AUTO:projects` span depends only on the registry, and the drift gate already fails any PR that edits the registry without regenerating it — so the only thing a nightly refresh could ever find is a change the gate had already blocked (`git log --grep="refresh README"` is empty). Its dispatch-only `escalate-attention` job duplicated the fleet doctor. `reconcile-registry.yml` now regenerates the span in its own PR, which is the one automated registry edit. In the same pass the six inline copies of `Report Claude run cost` became the `claude-cost` action (one had drifted to the wrong cap), the five inline token-probe loops became `resolve-fleet-token`, the four hand-rolled tracking-issue upserts became `upsert-issue`, the data loops' commits gained `[skip ci]` so a generated-data push no longer wakes five PR gates and a second site build, and `build-dash`'s cron moved to 08:37 — after the last data push — so the site is built once a day instead of three times.

#### Folded into `fleet-pulse.yml`

`actions-usage.yml`, `ai-usage.yml`, `daily-repo-analysis.yml`, and `actions-review.yml` were four workflows doing one job. Each paid for its own checkout and Python setup on its own cron, and they were chained by a `workflow_run` trigger matching a **display name** that had to be kept in sync by hand.

That chain broke silently. A ruleset was added to `main` ("Changes must be made through a pull request" + "Commits must have verified signatures"), the three data jobs' closing `git push` started being rejected, and because `actions-review.yml` triggered on `actions-usage.yml` *succeeding*, it stopped running too. Every generator still worked; the fleet's data froze for three weeks and nothing reported it.

Both structural causes are fixed in the replacement: publishing goes through [`utilities/publish-data`](../actions/utilities/publish-data/action.yml), which falls back to a pull request when a direct push is refused, and `doctor` is a `needs:` job rather than a separate `workflow_run` workflow, so it can't be skipped by an upstream publish failure. The generators themselves are unchanged and still available as `dash actions`, `dash ai-usage`, `dash daily`, `dash triage`, `dash actions-review`.

## Legacy / dispatch-only

`unified-evolution.yml` is the last of a generic single-app suite that only ever ran against the **root** tree (which has no app code — the projects are submodules). It is **`workflow_dispatch`-only** and still powers the manual AI evolution pass (trigger via `tools/dash evolve`).

The other four — `unified-cicd.yml`, `unified-release.yml`, `unified-maintenance.yml`, and `workflow-dispatcher.yml` (1,754 lines) — were **removed**: nothing in `tools/`, `.claude/`, or the docs invoked them, `workflow-dispatcher.yml` existed only to dispatch the other three, and every responsibility they nominally covered is served by a control-plane workflow above. Recover from git history if a reference implementation is ever wanted.

## Standards

- One workflow per durable responsibility; propagate shared CI via the `workflow_call` template, not by copying near-duplicate workflows.
- Top-level `permissions: contents: read`; elevate per-job only where needed.
- Every job sets `timeout-minutes`; every write-capable schedulable workflow has a `concurrency:` group.
- **Claude auth (house convention):** every `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` call site is preceded by the `claude-auth` step (`uses: bamr87/bamr87/.github/actions/claude-auth@main`, fed `vars.CLAUDE_AUTH_ORDER`). Each credential input is gated on the method it outputs, so the repo's `ai_auth` order in `_data/fleet.yml` decides which credential is used (default `oauth,api_key`). Canonical shape and provisioning: [`docs/AI-INTEGRATION.md`](../../docs/AI-INTEGRATION.md).
- **Claude spend (house convention):** every `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` call site also passes `--max-budget-usd` in its `claude_args`. `--max-turns` bounds *iterations*, not spend — one turn against a large context can outspend thirty small ones — so a turn cap is not a budget. The ceiling is declared once in [`_data/fleet.yml`](../../_data/fleet.yml) `budget.call_sites`, keyed `<workflow file>:<job id>`; because a `claude_args` string cannot read YAML, `.github/scripts/dash-gen/test_ai_budget.py` asserts that the literal and the declaration agree, that no call site is missing one, and that each cap clears `usd_per_turn × --max-turns`. Adding a Claude step without a cap fails that test. Every such step (bar the human-triggered `@claude` handler) is followed by a `Report Claude run cost` step — `id: cost`, `if: !cancelled()`, `uses: ./.github/actions/claude-cost` with the SAME cap as `budget-usd` — never an inline copy: six inline copies had drifted, one to the wrong cap. The action **exits non-zero** on a budget hit (an `::error::` annotation does not fail a job, and a green job runs every `success()`-gated step after it on truncated work), publishes `budget_hit` as an output for any step that would publish the agent's tree, echoes the result record into the run log so the cost collector still sees a run that aborted, and names a refused credential. A job whose workspace is another repository takes it from a sparse `.fleet-hub` checkout of the same commit (`./.fleet-hub/.github/actions/claude-cost`). Rationale: [`docs/AI-INTEGRATION.md`](../../docs/AI-INTEGRATION.md#spend-guardrails).
- **Bot identity:** automated commits use `bamr87-bot <10567847+bamr87@users.noreply.github.com>` (the noreply form is required by email-privacy push protection).
- **Never end a workflow in a bare `git push` to a protected branch.** Publish generated data through [`utilities/publish-data`](../actions/utilities/publish-data/action.yml), which pushes directly when allowed and opens a stable-branch PR when it isn't. The publish route is a property of the *repository* and can change without warning; resolving it at runtime is what stops a settings change from decapitating the automation. This is not hypothetical — it already happened once and cost three weeks of fleet data.
- **Prefer `needs:` over `workflow_run`.** A `workflow_run` trigger couples workflows by display-name string and silently skips the downstream when the upstream fails for *any* reason — including a reason unrelated to the data it produces.
- **A multi-stage loop reconciles state; it does not replay events.** Where a workflow advances work through stages (`issue-pipeline.yml`), the stage must live somewhere durable and human-editable — labels, not an implicit event chain. Every run then acts on current state, so a cancelled run or a missed webhook costs one cycle of latency instead of wedging an item forever, and a human can re-queue or stop anything by editing one label.
- **A PR that must have CI cannot be opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.** GitHub does not fire workflow events for refs pushed with it, so the PR arrives with no checks — and anything downstream that reads those checks silently has nothing to read. Use `FLEET_TOKEN`, and **probe it** (`gh api user`) rather than testing that it is merely set: a present-but-expired PAT has degraded this fleet's automation before without warning.
- **Toolchain versions come from `vars.*`, not literals.** Reusable workflows resolve caller input → the calling repo's `vars.NODE_VERSION`/`PYTHON_VERSION`/`RUBY_VERSION` → a built-in default, so `dash config sync` can bump the fleet from `_data/fleet.yml`.
- **Token contract:** declared in [`_data/fleet.yml`](../../_data/fleet.yml). `FLEET_TOKEN` is the single fine-grained PAT the control plane uses fleet-wide (the legacy per-loop PATs are gone — `FANOUT_TOKEN` on 2026-09-30, `ACTIONS_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` / `DAILY_ANALYSIS_TOKEN` on 2026-10-19). Every workflow resolves it the same way: `uses: ./.github/actions/resolve-fleet-token`, which probes it with `GET /user`, exports the winner as `GH_TOKEN`, and takes `github.token` as the unprobed last resort only where the caller passes `default-token` — a loop that cannot deliver without the PAT (repo-evolution, the fan-out, git-digs) passes none and fails before spending anything. Audit with `dash secrets`; rotate with `dash secrets rotate`.
- **A credential nobody re-writes is a credential nobody knows the age of.** Fleet-wide secrets are provisioned and refreshed by `token-rotation.yml`, not placed by hand: the loop reads each repo's age from GitHub's `updated_at` (the API returns names and timestamps but never values, which is exactly what an audit needs) and writes hub-first, aborting the fan-out if the hub refuses — a bad credential on one repo is an incident, on all 41 it is an outage. Never log, echo, or commit a secret value; the only channel one travels is an env var in and `gh secret set`'s stdin out.
- Fan-outs go through `tools/fanout.sh` (dry-run default, PRs only, external-upstream guard) — don't inline new clone→seed→PR loops.
- **One tracking issue per concern, updated in place, closed when clean:** file it with `uses: ./.github/actions/utilities/upsert-issue` (exact-title dedupe, labels created on demand, `state: close` to retire it), never a hand-rolled `gh issue list | create` — four copies of that each grew their own duplicate-issue bug. Alarms (`api-keys`, the rotation report) are filed with `github.token` on purpose: an alarm must not ride on the credential most likely to be dead.
- **Generated-data commits carry `[skip ci]`.** A data push (fleet-pulse, issue-pipeline, token-rotation, update-submodules) needs none of the PR gates; `build-dash.yml`'s cron republishes the site after the last one. The nightly `python-tests.yml` run is what still verifies `main` after they land.
- **A job whose workspace is another repository** (repo-evolution's `evolve`, the fan-out's `agent-fill`, `fleet-verify.yml`) takes the hub's composite actions from a sparse checkout of the hub at the same commit — `./.fleet-hub/.github/actions/<name>` — hidden from git in `.git/info/exclude`, never from a floating tag.
- Avoid scheduled write-capable workflows unless the owner confirmed perms/secrets.
- Update this README when adding, removing, or renaming workflows.

## Validation

`actionlint` runs in CI (drift-check.yml) and locally: `actionlint` from the repo root. Also check that referenced local actions/scripts exist.
